claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite the unresolved Spanish-language billing support evaluation gap.

concern_ledger.concern: Material Spanish-language billing support gap remains unresolved for a segment named in three international pilot commitments.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence that the gap has been remediated to target or is no longer present for the named segment.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy treats named launch use cases and customer commitments as material; certification cannot rely on aggregate readiness alone once a material limitation is identified.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows disclosure of the material limitation before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Completed launch disclosure artifact or equivalent admissible evidence showing the limitation was disclosed before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The release policy expressly requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the material limitation.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Approved risk-acceptance record specifically covering the Spanish-language billing support gap for the named commitments.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Absent resolution or disclosure, approved risk acceptance is the only remaining policy path identified in the record.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review on disclosure remains pending with no final answer.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Final legal disposition confirming required disclosure has been handled or is unnecessary based on a completed admissible analysis consistent with policy.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The policy text says product labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending; the unresolved legal predicate prevents a compliant certification record.

decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the material limitation is either resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
A weakness affecting a named customer commitment or named launch use case is material under the stated policy, regardless of product labeling it non-core or low-volume.
General aggregate readiness evidence can support launch readiness, but it cannot substitute for a policy-required disclosure or approved risk acceptance on a material limitation.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the Spanish-language billing support gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the required disclosure for the named launch use case has been completed before launch.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering this specific material limitation if disclosure will not occur before launch.
Evidence that the evaluation gap has been resolved to target before launch if the actor relies on remediation instead of disclosure or risk acceptance.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a 2.1 percentage point miss in Spanish-language billing support for a segment named in three international pilot commitments, which meets the policy's materiality trigger for named launch use cases.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no admissible evidence shows either condition is satisfied.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so the required policy predicate is unresolved at the time of certification.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure the separate disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement for a material limitation.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on current evidence merely because aggregate launch readiness is positive and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred.
That public model-card and AI risk-management guidance is sufficient support for certification under the internal release policy despite the unresolved materiality and disclosure issue.
